record_verbatim.evidence: Three figures in the corpus disagree about the same reaction. FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 states: acceptance criterion 'Contactor open latency, Time from FAULT request to contactor feedback open, 30 ms'; rationale '30 ms mechanical opening + 5 ms feedback = 35 ms within FTTI budget'; and the safety goal's timing_budget.allocation gives contactor_command 5 + contactor_mechanical 30 + feedback_verification 5 = 40 ms after the fault request. The requirement's own threshold is therefore 10 ms tighter than its own arithmetic and 5 ms tighter than the budget it is spending from. FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 also states a 5 ms coil de-energise criterion, which is consistent with the 5 ms contactor_command allocation, so the requirement is internally coherent on the command and incoherent on the completion.
record_verbatim.impact: A requirement whose threshold is tighter than its own mechanism's budget will fail, and when it fails the failure will look like a defect in the contactor driver rather than a defect in the requirement, so the engineering effort goes to the wrong place. It also makes the safety goal's 100 ms interval unverifiable at the end of the chain: the existing acceptance criteria, taken together, claim a reaction that is faster than the sum of the recorded parts. Any verification measure written against FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 inherits an unachievable threshold.

record_verbatim.resolution:
RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected from 'accepted' to 'resolved'. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: FB2-SAF-FSR-000003's acceptance criteria now carry 'Contactor open latency / Time from FAULT request to contactor feedback open (auxiliary contacts confirm open) / 40 ms', plus a separate 'Contactor mechanically open latency' criterion at 35 ms and a 'Coil de-energise to mechanically open' criterion at 30 ms that asks for FB2-PRM-000005's value under its own label.

The reasoning this record used still holds and is the reason the fix is not a loose number: 30 ms is the mechanical opening time alone, 35 ms is command-plus-actuation and was wrong where it appeared because it omitted the 5 ms coil-command segment the same requirement budgets separately, and 40 ms is the figure for the quantity the criterion actually names. The threshold was made HARDER to claim compliance with, not easier, and the real foxBMS source was consulted first and cannot settle the number - CONT_OpenContactor carries no timing constant - so FB2-PRM-000005 is the authority and it was not edited. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.
